lev.source: India's updated NDC press release (PIB PRID 1847812 dated 3 Aug 2022); draft National Electricity Policy 2026
lev.how_used_in_model: Net-zero-aligned variant: direct CO2 intensity of the grid must stay under a path from 0.67 t/MWh (FY2025-26) to zero in 2070 (front-loaded exponent 1.5; linear path used as minimum test)
lev.status: Verified (target); the path shape is OUR assumption

lev.source: India's updated NDC (PIB PRID 1847812); draft NEP 2026
lev.how_used_in_model: Not modelled directly (economy-wide and GDP-based). Reported as context; grid intensity is the generation-based proxy

lev.value_and_year: about 50% by 2030 (60% by 2035 per CAT summary)
lev.source: India's updated NDC (PIB PRID 1847812); Climate Action Tracker
lev.how_used_in_model: Capacity-based: NOT used as an input. Cross-checked only through the NEP/NGAP solar and wind plans below
lev.status: Verified (2030 wording); 2035 figure from CAT summary

lev.value_and_year: NEP 2023: solar 311 GW, wind 82 GW by 2031-32; CEA NGAP 2026: 320 GW + 103 GW by 2031-32 and 509 GW + 155 GW by 2035-36
lev.source: Climate Action Tracker summary of CEA NEP 2023 and NGAP 2026
lev.how_used_in_model: 'Current policies', 'Net-zero' and 'Viksit Bharat' variants: converted to energy (GW x load factor 22% solar / 30% wind x 8760 h) = 887 TWh in 2032 and 1388 TWh in 2036 and used as a FLOOR on wind+solar generation. Load factors are our assumption. Use is generation-equivalent, not a capacity forecast
lev.status: Plans verified via CAT summary (not the primary CEA documents)

lev.value_and_year: 22.38 GW by 2031-32; 100 GW by 2047; at least 5 indigenous SMRs by 2033
lev.source: PIB feature article (28 Feb 2026) quoting NPCIL/DAE; draft NEP 2026 and SHANTI Act 2025 as reported by World Nuclear News
lev.how_used_in_model: 9% of generation in 2047 in the main case (organisers confirmed); 100 GW x 80% load factor = 700 TWh in the nuclear-ambition, net-zero and Viksit Bharat variants; 22.38 GW x 80% = 157 TWh by 2032 in policy variants
lev.status: Verified (targets); load factor is our assumption

lev.value_and_year: Developed-country ambition; draft NEP: per-person electricity above 4000 kWh by 2047
lev.source: Draft National Electricity Policy 2026 (reported by SCC Online / WNN)
lev.how_used_in_model: High-growth demand scenario (Step 1) plus the 'Viksit Bharat build-out' variant: faster wind+solar ramp (12%/yr), nuclear 100 GW, higher storage/grid limit (75%), carbon price Rs 500/tCO2. The consumption figure is NOT used (brief bans consumption for comparison)
lev.status: Verified (targets); build-out parameters are our assumptions

lev.value_and_year: CEA/NEP 2023: about 236 GWh battery storage by 2030 (CAT summary); Energy Storage Obligation (about 4% by 2029-30) appears dropped in latest RPO revision; draft NEP 2026: no numeric storage target found in summaries
lev.source: Climate Action Tracker; Mercom (25 Oct 2023 headline); SCC Online
lev.how_used_in_model: Represented by the limit on wind+solar share of generation (0.30 rising to 0.65 by 2047; 0.75 Viksit; 0.80 net-zero). Storage is not modelled explicitly
lev.status: Partly verified. DRAFT NEP storage wording NOT found - do not cite

lev.value_and_year: No plans to close coal plants before 2030; about 23 GW under construction and 107 GW pre-construction (Jan 2026)
lev.how_used_in_model: Coal generation cannot fall more than 1% a year until 2030, then at most 6% a year (assumption)
lev.status: Statement verified via CAT; 6% limit is our assumption

lev.value_and_year: CCTS (India's carbon market) uses intensity targets and initially excludes the power sector
lev.how_used_in_model: Carbon price added to coal and gas costs in the scoring: Rs 1000/tCO2 net-zero variant, Rs 500 Viksit variant, 0 otherwise (illustrative, no official price)
lev.status: Scheme verified; the price is our assumption

lev.value_and_year: 5 MMT/yr by 2030 supported by about 125 GW dedicated renewable capacity
lev.source: PIB (28 Feb 2026) and Climate Action Tracker
lev.how_used_in_model: NOT added to demand (Step 1 totals are trend-based). Sensitivity: 5 MMT x about 52 kWh/kg = about 260 TWh at full delivery; 20% delivery = about 52 TWh by 2030
lev.status: Target verified; electricity use per kg is a standard engineering value (not sourced here)

lev.value_and_year: Government aim of 15% gas in the energy mix by 2030
